clue.text: Hitchhiker's guide?

parts.note: the thing that guides a hitchhiker is the digit stuck out at the roadside, read here as a phrase for a practical guideline

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a nod to a famous travel book, but the guide is the hitchhiker's raised digit, and the phrase that names it also means a rough practical rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough working principle based on experience is called this idiom, and a hitchhiker literally relies on the digit it names.

clue.text: Lives on the borders

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning on or concerning
the borders of something are its sides or edges

explanation.surface: Someone lives out on the edge of the country, in border territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the borders' reads as where someone lives; 'on' here is the RE of a letter heading, as in 're: your order'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there; the verb forms match as third person singular.

clue.text: Lifts the seat up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for seat is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a stool is a simple seat with no back

explanation.surface: Someone raises the seat, perhaps the toilet seat, with a cheeky exclamation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifts' looks like the action on the seat, but it is the definition in its slang sense of steals.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift is slang for to steal, and plunders or pilfers are synonyms of the verb meaning to take goods unlawfully.

clue.text: In bloom, but not at home

definitions.meaning: flowers that have opened are said to be fully open, in flower
someone who has gone elsewhere is absent from the house

explanation.definitionFit: Opened blossoms are said to be this, and a person who has left the house is also described with the same short word.

clue.text: Understand it's only a small branch

definitions.meaning: informal British usage: to catch on or grasp a point
a slender shoot growing from a tree's bough

explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to grasp a point is to catch on; a slender woody shoot is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Nations tried and found "not proven"

parts.note: UN is short for the United Nations
something tried out has been tested

explanation.surface: The nations of the world sat in judgement and returned the verdict 'not proven'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not proven' is a Scottish court verdict, which steers the solver towards a trial; here it simply means never put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never put through a trial or check has not been shown to work, so it remains unverified.

clue.text: Discard travel game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Throw out the board game you take on journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travel game' reads as one thing, a game for car journeys, but 'travel' gives GO and 'game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbers-calling game of chance played with cards in halls is an example of a game.

clue.text: Pours scorn on issue put about free

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the turned word goes on either side of the word for free
put is read as in 'put about', turning a ship round, so the word for issue is set the other way

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants, as in biblical 'issue'
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a publication that was handed out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, not a magazine issue. 'put' (as in a ship put about) reverses it, giving DEES, and 'about' wraps those letters round the word for free.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or ridicule someone is to pour scorn on them.

clue.text: Is it done as new issues?

indicators.note: new tells the solver to make something fresh out of these letters by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is acceptable to treat old publications as brand new ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' sits beside 'issues' as if describing them, but it is the anagram signal for IS IT DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Different printings of a book or newspaper are its separate issues.

clue.text: Selected applicants have little inclination

parts.note: short means little in height or length
a list is a ship's lean or tilt to one side

explanation.surface: The chosen job applicants have little desire to proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' tempts as desire, but it is the nautical sense: a list is a ship's tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The candidates picked out for interview from a larger field form a final selection list.

clue.text: Day spent in rain storm is the low point

indicators.note: something spent in a place is passed inside it, so the letter for day goes inside
storm suggests turbulence, so the letters of rain are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Spending a day out in a rainstorm is the worst part of the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' turns RAIN into ANIR, and 'spent in' puts D (day) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point, opposite to the zenith, is the astronomical term used figuratively for the worst moment.

clue.text: Condescend to accept his final plan

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the chosen letter goes inside

parts.note: to deign is to condescend to do something

indicators.note: final points to the last letter of the word his

explanation.surface: Someone stoops so low as to approve his final scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or plan drawn up for something.

clue.text: Gather there's action starting in the valley

indicators.note: in means the first letter of action is placed inside the word for valley

parts.note: a glen is a Scottish word for a narrow valley

indicators.note: starting means only the opening letter of the word action is used

explanation.surface: Gather round, there is something happening in the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: GLEN is a valley, especially in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect bit by bit, like picking up leftover grain after harvest, is to gather.

clue.text: Various trades so represented

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, laid out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A range of trades are represented this way at a fair or union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' reads as being present at a meeting, but here it means presented anew: the letters of TRADES SO rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed collection of different kinds is described as various, or of many sorts.

clue.text: What one 2 is!

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer to 2 down, a verb meaning lifts or pinches; the thing one takes that way has been taken unlawfully

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference borrows 2 down's answer, which means lifts in the sense of pilfers; whatever one lifts is therefore taken property.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that have been pilfered or pinched are described as taken without permission, the past participle of steal.

clue.text: Finished the lottery — go into the red

parts.note: something that is over has finished
a lottery is a prize draw

explanation.surface: Once the lottery was over with no win, the gambler slipped into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' means in debt, from red ink once used for losses in accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out more than your bank balance holds puts the account in debt, idiomatically going into the red.

clue.text: International organization that makes communist angry

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A global body whose actions infuriate a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide humanitarian movement is an example of an international organization.

clue.text: A large number boasted lack of energy

indicators.note: lack of means a letter is missing from the word for boasted

parts.note: to crow is to boast, so boasted gives crowed
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Many people bragged but were too tired to back it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng or mass of people is a large number gathered together.

clue.text: Short tea break for the current controller

indicators.note: break means the letters of short tea are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A brief tea break for the person who runs things at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current controller' suggests the boss of the moment, but current is electrical: the device is a variable resistor.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable resistor used to regulate electrical flow controls current, as in a dimmer switch.

clue.text: Disorderly — he's a drunk with no right to have a knife

indicators.note: disorderly suggests a messy jumble, so the remaining letters are shuffled
with no means a letter is taken away from the drunken phrase

parts.note: taken as written, he is a drunk

explanation.surface: A rowdy drunk has no right to carry a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The SKEAN DHU is the small dagger worn in the sock of Scottish Highland dress. Remove R from HE'S A DRUNK, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This Highland dagger, tucked into the stocking with a kilt, is a kind of knife.

clue.text: Homer is up before members, performing!

indicators.note: before means the reversed piece comes ahead of the rest
in a down clue, up means the word is is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: The poet Homer is rising ahead of other members of a performing troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' suggests the Greek poet, but it is Homer Simpson of the cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The father in the long-running American cartoon family is named Homer, so his first name stands for his surname.

clue.text: One sat outside, with equanimity

indicators.note: outside means the word for sat goes round the letter for one

parts.note: to pose is to sit for a portrait, so sat gives posed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sat outdoors, perfectly calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sat' means sat for an artist: posed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being composed and self-possessed means keeping calm, which is having equanimity.

clue.text: Arrange the queen's furniture

parts.note: to dress is to arrange, as a shop window is dressed
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Lay out the queen's furniture in her palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard with shelves for dishes is an item of furniture.

clue.text: A go-between from television and radio, say, backing rubbish

parts.note: television and radio are examples of the media

indicators.note: backing means the word for rubbish is written in reverse

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A broadcaster acting as intermediary backs a load of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who negotiates between two parties in a dispute is a go-between.

clue.text: Jelly, when on plates in cooking starters

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: starters means the opening letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A jelly put on plates as the cooking's opening course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like first courses in a kitchen, but it picks out the first letters P, I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury gelatin made from meat stock is a kind of jelly.

clue.text: Counsel notice moral shortcoming

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a vice is a moral failing

explanation.surface: Legal counsel notices a defect of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a lawyer but is the noun meaning guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel in the sense of recommendation or guidance offered to someone is a synonym.

clue.text: Single distribution of cards that's fanciful

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, hence single
a deal is the handing out of cards

explanation.surface: Dealing out a single hand of cards is a fanciful idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing only as a perfect imagined notion rather than in reality makes something fanciful.

clue.text: Just grounds for amusement

definitions.meaning: a funfair, a site with rides and stalls

explanation.definitionFit: Being even-handed is being just; a travelling funfair with rides occupies grounds for amusement.

clue.text: Crawled quietly to the bog?

parts.note: to do the front crawl is to swim, so crawled gives swam
P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone crept silently to the loo, bog being British slang for toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawled' suggests creeping, and 'bog' British slang for the toilet; but crawled means swam the crawl stroke, and bog is marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh or wet spongy ground is a bog.

clue.text: Childish impressions of footballers changing?

definitions.meaning: pictures that children press onto paper or skin, like decals
footballers moving from one club to another

explanation.definitionFit: Decals children rub onto paper are one kind; players moving between clubs for a fee are the other.

clue.text: Runner's case of shock in front of one

indicators.note: in front of means the outer letters come before the letter for one
case of means the outside letters of shock, its first and last letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An athlete suffers a bout of shock ahead of one rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is one of a pair of runners on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow runner fitted to the feet for gliding over snow is one of a pair used in winter sport.

clue.text: Larva often found on building sites?

definitions.meaning: the grub stage of a butterfly or moth
a tracked earth-moving vehicle, or one made by the US machinery maker of that name

explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly's grub stage is this; tracked bulldozers and diggers on construction sites carry the same name.
